name: HubSpot
one_liner: HubSpot is a CRM-based customer platform combining marketing, sales, service, content and data hubs with built-in AI agents, plus a broad developer platform with REST APIs and apps.

auth.note: OAuth for multi-account apps, static auth tokens for single account, developer API keys

access.note: Install CLI, authorize account and start building; Sign up available

mcp.note: Official remote MCP server at mcp.hubspot.com
Remote and local developer MCP servers

verdict.note: Documented OAuth and private app token auth for API calls

notes: Free developer signup is implied by the docs (Sign up button, hs init), but pricing/terms were not fetched. Installing apps in customer accounts may require permissions; the pages do not state admin requirements. Legacy private app tokens are also supported.

name: Firecrawl
one_liner: Firecrawl is an open-source web data API that lets AI agents search, scrape, crawl, map and interact with web pages and returns clean markdown or structured JSON.

auth.note: Bearer API key; OAuth for apps; keyless endpoints

access.note: Free plan with no card required

api_surface.note: v2 endpoints: search, scrape, interact, parse, monitor, crawl, map, agent

mcp.note: Official hosted MCP server with keyless, OAuth and API key options

verdict.note: Documented REST API with self-serve API key

notes: OAuth for apps is documented, but its details were not fetched. Some endpoints (v2 scrape, search, parse) also work keylessly with limits. Official SDKs exist alongside the raw REST API. Open-source self-hosting is also available.

name: fanbasis
one_liner: FanBasis (now Commas) is an all-in-one payments and checkout platform for creators and digital businesses, with BNPL, subscriptions, payouts, affiliates, and enterprise APIs.

auth.note: API docs are behind a password login; auth methods not visible.
Mentions API keys and webhooks in onboarding, but no auth documentation.

access.note: Enterprise API access comes with a dedicated implementation engineer, which suggests a sales-assisted flow.

api_surface.note: Marketing page claims a REST API, SDKs, a Postman collection, webhooks and a sandbox.

mcp.note: Vendor homepage lists an MCP (beta) for checkout links, refunds and metrics.

verdict.note: Docs are gated behind a login, so the interface cannot be verified.

notes: Auth is undocumented in the fetched pages. API docs are password-gated. The REST API and SDKs are claimed only on marketing pages. The MCP is a vague 'beta' mention on commas.com with no server or docs URL. Product appears rebranded from FanBasis to Commas. Access path (self-serve vs sales) is unclear.
